title: Brampton teen's cause of death following interaction with Toronto police officers undetermined says SIU
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has provided an update into its investigation of the death of a 19-year-old Brampton resident following an interaction with two members of the Toronto Police Service (TPS).
According to the SIU , the teen met with two persons in the Highway 50 and Bellchase Trail area of Brampton on April 26 "to conduct a business transaction."
Shortly after the transaction, the two purchasers realized the item purchased was "counterfeit" and proceeded to chase and catch the teen.
The SIU has confirmed that the two people buying the item are current officers with the TPS but were off duty at the time of the incident.
It is unknown what occurred after the officers caught the teen, with the SIU saying these details are not yet known.
Some time after this interaction, the teen's friend picked him and "noticed he appeared unwell."
However, the SIU would not comment on how the teen looked or what he was experiencing.
The friends brought the teen to a hospital where he later died, said the SIU's report.
Now, the agency is saying the cause of death of the teen is "undetermined at this time," with its latest update on Aug. 30.
The teen's identity has not yet been public made to "protect the privacy of the family," said the SIU.
In the original update published on Aug. 30, the SIU said a post-mortem was conducted on April 13 but retracted the statement, citing an error with the dates.
In terms of the officers, media spokesperson for the TPS, Connie Osbourne, confirmed neither have been suspended and are both on active duty.
Toronto Police said they were made aware of the death "last week" by Peel Regional Police and notified the SIU "within the hour."
The original investigation was started by Peel Regional Police, who turned over the case after learning the two suspects were officers with the TPS.
The SIU has yet to respond to the Brampton Guardian's questions about what the item purchased by the officers were, when or if a post-mortem was conducted or if either officer was interviewed.
Subject officers in a SIU investigation are not required to be interviewed or turn over their notes. They can only be asked to participate and can refuse to do so.
